text:
incidents-bot: AUTOPAGE fired: inference-gateway error-rate spike (5xx) in us-west1. alert link: https://pd.example.com/incidents/INC12345 — metric: gateway.5xx.rate > 3% over 2m. routed to oncall.
PagerDuty: Page created for @Rosa O (oncall). Escalation policy: inference-prod -> eng-sre.
Rosa O (oncall): ack. I'm on it — jumping into logs and topologies.
Tom H: seeing a sharp jump starting ~23:45 UTC. Looks correlated with canary traffic to model-rev-b.
Aisha K: confirm — k/v cache evictions spike around same time: kvcache.evictions per-second increased x10.
Mira L: is this causing the 502/503, or is backend timeout? quick check: tail gateway logs.
Tom H: pasted snippet: ```
[23:46:01] inference-gateway ERROR upstream timeout for request id=abc123 status=502 latency=1200ms route=/v1/generate
[23:46:03] kvcache WARN evict key=model-rev-b-prefix size=48MB
```
DevOps Dave: can we divert canary traffic back to stable for quick test? if it's canary config bug then rollback should reduce error rate.
Rosa O (oncall): initiating canary rollback now via console. command: `redwood deploy rollback --env=prod --service=canary-router --to=stable`
incidents-bot: deploy rollback job started (job id: jb_7782). Estimated 30s.
Tom H: I can also scale up dedicated pool for inference-gateway to reduce timeouts while rollback completes: `kubectl scale deployment inference-gw --replicas=6 -n prod`. Doing it.
Aisha K: warming a small warmup of model-rev-b on stable nodes to avoid cold misses. sending synthetic traffic.
Mira L: quick sanity: rolling average 5xx now 2.9% (down from 6.1%). P95 latency improved slightly.
Rosa O (oncall): rollback finished, job jb_7782 status=success.
incidents-bot: monitor update: error-rate now 1.2% over 1m.
Tom H: looks like rollback removed the bad canary config — we should still validate root cause. I captured canary config diff: `keepalive.max_conns` was reduced unintentionally to 20 for model-rev-b. That caused connection churn and cache thrash.
Aisha K: hypothesis fits kvcache evictions spike. If keepalive too low, clients reauthenticate and thrash cache entries.
Mira L: customer impact check: query sampling shows ~18k failed requests in the 20 min window across prod, concentrated in us-west1. Affected customers approx 12 (higher throughput tenants). Support can reach out if needed.
Rosa O (oncall): immediate mitigation done (rollback + scale). Next steps: rollback permanent, add canary alert for keepalive changes, temp raise keepalive on stable to 100, add synthetic post-deploy check for kvcache eviction spike.
DevOps Dave: filing a follow-up ticket: RW-INC-2024-099 — owner Tom H, due EOD tomorrow. It will include reproducer steps, config audit, and canary gating.
Tom H: also adding a short-term guard in deployment pipeline to block keepalive < 50 for inference routes.
Aisha K: I'll draft the customer-facing blurb for support. Suggest: "Between 23:45–00:05 UTC some requests to inference endpoints in us-west1 experienced elevated 5xx errors due to a canary config change; traffic was rolled back and normal behavior restored. We're contacting affected customers."
Mira L: metrics to attach for postmortem: total failed requests: 18,432, peak 5xx rate 6.1%, regions: us-west1, impacted routes: /v1/generate.
Rosa O (oncall): handoff to next oncall in 30m — leaving notes in PD and will create runbook checklist.
Tom H: brief diagnostic commands used so folks can replay: ```
# fetch gateway errors
kubectl logs -l app=inference-gateway -n prod --since=30m | grep ERROR | head -n 50
# check kvcache stats
redwood-kvstat --cluster=us-west1 --metric=evictions --window=30m
```
incidents-bot: Reminder: create postmortem within 72h.
Rosa O (oncall): final check: current 5xx rate 0.4% over 5m — stabilized. I'll update the PD incident status to resolved after handoff. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
Mira L: thumbs. I'll add the graphs to the incident ticket.
DevOps Dave: added RW-INC-2024-099 and linked to PD. Owner assigned.
Aisha K: Support blurb ready, will send to CSMs for affected accounts.
Rosa O (oncall): handing off to Tom H for follow-up. Tagging @Tom H.
Tom H: taking follow-up ownership. leaving notes: reproduce locally using canary traffic generator, audit pipeline, add gating and synthetic checks.
Rosa O (oncall): resolved. closing thread. :lock:
